items.q: I ______ this novel since Monday, and I still haven't reached the last chapter.
items.vi: Tôi đọc cuốn tiểu thuyết này từ thứ Hai mà vẫn chưa tới chương cuối.
items.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on (since Monday + still haven't reached) takes the present perfect continuous: have been reading. ✗ am reading — present continuous is only for now, it cannot take since + a starting point; ✗ read — past simple means the reading is finished, but it is still going on; ✗ was reading — past continuous puts the action in the past, not reaching up to now.

items.q: Lan: How much is the bus ______ to the cinema? / Nam: Only seven thousand dong each way.
items.vi: Lan: Vé xe buýt tới rạp chiếu phim bao nhiêu tiền? / Nam: Chỉ bảy nghìn đồng một chiều thôi.
items.explanation: The money for a bus, taxi or train ride is a fare — the clue is bus + each way. ✗ fee — money for a professional service (doctor, school, lawyer); ✗ price — the cost of goods in a shop, not of a journey; ✗ charge — a general amount a company asks for a service, not the fixed word for transport.

items.q: My parents ______ for my sister's wedding party: a live band, fireworks and a five-tier cake.
items.vi: Bố mẹ tôi đã dốc toàn lực cho tiệc cưới của chị tôi: ban nhạc sống, pháo hoa và chiếc bánh cưới năm tầng.
items.explanation: The list a live band, fireworks and a five-tier cake shows every possible effort, which is pull out all the stops = do everything possible to make something a success. ✗ pulled some strings — used secret influence to get a favour; ✗ pulled their socks up — started to work harder; ✗ pulled our legs — joked with us, made us believe something untrue.

items.q: My brother ______ the housework on Saturdays while I cook lunch.
items.vi: Anh tôi làm việc nhà vào thứ Bảy còn tôi nấu bữa trưa.
items.explanation: Housework collocates with do: we do the housework, the shopping, the washing-up (routine tasks). ✗ makes — make goes with things you create (a cake, a decision, a mess), not routine chores; ✗ takes — take pairs with a photo, a break, a bus, never housework; ✗ gives — give pairs with a hand, a speech, a present, never housework.

items.q: That's the singer ______ concert we went to last month.
items.vi: Đó là ca sĩ mà tháng trước chúng tôi đã đi xem buổi hòa nhạc của cô ấy.
items.explanation: The concert belongs to the singer, so the blank needs the possessive relative whose + noun (whose concert). ✗ who — a subject pronoun for a person, but the clause already has its subject we; ✗ whom — an object pronoun for a person, and it cannot stand before the noun concert; ✗ which — refers to a thing, but here the antecedent is the person singer.

items.q: Minh's birthday party has been ______ until next Saturday because his mother is ill.
items.vi: Tiệc sinh nhật của Minh đã bị hoãn đến thứ Bảy tuần sau vì mẹ cậu ấy bị ốm.
items.explanation: Put off = postpone, which is what until next Saturday + his mother is ill describe. ✗ put out — extinguish a fire or a light; ✗ put up — build (a tent), raise (prices) or give someone a bed for the night; ✗ set off — start a journey, and a party cannot set off.

items.q: To save money, my friends and I stayed at a cheap ______ where we shared a room with six other travellers.
items.vi: Để tiết kiệm tiền, tôi và bạn bè ở một nhà nghỉ tập thể giá rẻ, chung phòng với sáu du khách khác.
items.explanation: A hostel is cheap accommodation where travellers share big rooms — the clues are cheap and shared a room with six other travellers. ✗ hotel — you get your own room, and it is not typically cheap; ✗ resort — an expensive holiday complex with private rooms; ✗ campsite — you sleep in a tent, not in a room.

items.q: Nam ______ the film last night — he was at my house until midnight.
items.vi: Nam không thể nào đã xem bộ phim tối qua được — cậu ấy ở nhà tôi đến tận nửa đêm.
items.explanation: Can't have + past participle = it was impossible in the past; the clue he was at my house until midnight makes seeing the film impossible. ✗ must have seen — near certainty that it DID happen, the opposite of the evidence; ✗ might have seen — a possibility, but the evidence rules it out; ✗ should have seen — an action that was expected but not done, a regret, not a deduction.

items.q: There were only ______ guests at the party, so we all sat around one table.
items.vi: Bữa tiệc chỉ có vài vị khách, nên tất cả chúng tôi ngồi quanh một bàn.
items.explanation: Guests is a countable plural and only + a few = a small number, which explains one table. ✗ few — already means "almost none" (negative), so it is not used after only; ✗ little — goes with uncountable nouns (little time), not with guests; ✗ a little — also uncountable only (a little sugar), not for people you can count.

items.q: By the time we found our seats, the film ______.
items.vi: Lúc chúng tôi tìm được chỗ ngồi thì bộ phim đã bắt đầu rồi.
items.explanation: By the time + past simple (found) needs the past perfect for the action that happened first: had already started. ✗ has already started — present perfect links to now, but the story is in the past; ✗ already starts — present simple cannot follow a past-time clause; ✗ is already starting — present continuous describes now, not an earlier past moment.

items.q: After the doctor's visit, my father decided ______ smoking for good.
items.vi: Sau khi đi khám bác sĩ, bố tôi quyết định bỏ hẳn thuốc lá.
items.explanation: Decide is followed by a to-infinitive: decided to give up. ✗ giving up — a gerund, but decide is not a gerund verb (unlike stop / enjoy); ✗ give up — a bare infinitive only follows modals or make / let, not decide; ✗ to giving up — to + -ing exists only after set phrases like look forward to, never after decide.

items.q: From our hotel balcony we had a wonderful ______ of the harbour.
items.vi: Từ ban công khách sạn, chúng tôi ngắm được toàn cảnh bến cảng thật tuyệt.
items.explanation: Have a view of is the pattern for what you can see from a place, and from our hotel balcony gives the viewpoint. ✗ sight — the ability to see, or a place tourists visit (the sights), not what a balcony offers; ✗ scene — a part of a film or play, or the place where something happens; ✗ scenery — uncountable, so it can never take a.

items.q: ______ the film was three hours long, nobody left the cinema early.
items.vi: Mặc dù bộ phim dài ba tiếng, không ai rời rạp sớm cả.
items.explanation: The blank introduces a full clause (the film was three hours long) that contrasts with nobody left early, so the conjunction is although. ✗ Despite — a preposition, it needs a noun or -ing (despite the film being long), not subject + verb; ✗ However — an adverb that starts a new sentence, it cannot join two clauses with a comma; ✗ Because — gives a reason, but a long film is not a reason for staying.

items.q: The picnic was cancelled because of the ______ rain on Sunday morning.
items.vi: Buổi dã ngoại bị hủy vì trận mưa lớn sáng Chủ nhật.
items.explanation: Rain, traffic and snow are described as heavy = falling in large amounts. ✗ strong — collocates with wind, coffee or a smell, not rain; ✗ hard — "it rained hard" is an adverb, but hard rain before the noun is not the standard collocation; ✗ big — used for size (a big storm), never for rain.

items.q: Dad finally ______ and said that nobody could use a phone at the dinner table.
options: put his cards on the table
items.vi: Cuối cùng bố cũng cương quyết ra lệnh rằng không ai được dùng điện thoại trong bữa tối.
items.explanation: Put your foot down = be firm and refuse to allow something, which matches the strict rule nobody could use a phone. ✗ put his feet up — relax, rest; ✗ put his back into it — work very hard at a task; ✗ put his cards on the table — be honest and open about your plans.

items.q: If my brother ______ so much noise every evening, I could finish my book in a week.
items.vi: Nếu em trai tôi không làm ồn như vậy mỗi tối thì tôi có thể đọc xong cuốn sách trong một tuần.
items.explanation: A second conditional describes a present situation that is not true — every evening + could finish — so the if-clause takes the past simple: didn't make. ✗ doesn't make — present simple belongs to the first conditional with will / can, not could; ✗ hadn't made — past perfect is the third conditional about a finished past event, which clashes with every evening; ✗ won't make — will is not used in an if-clause.

items.q: Our ______ was a quiet village by the sea, but the bus dropped us in the wrong town.
items.vi: Điểm đến của chúng tôi là một ngôi làng yên tĩnh ven biển, nhưng xe buýt lại thả chúng tôi ở nhầm thị trấn.
items.explanation: The place you are travelling to is your destination; the clue is the contrast with the wrong town. ✗ direction — the way you go (north, left), not a place; ✗ distance — how far it is, a length, not a village; ✗ arrival — the act of getting somewhere, not the place itself.

items.q: Neither my parents nor my little sister ______ horror films.
items.vi: Cả bố mẹ tôi lẫn em gái tôi đều không thích phim kinh dị.
items.explanation: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it: singular my little sister → likes. ✗ like — plural, it would agree with parents, which is further from the verb; ✗ are liking — plural AND a continuous form, but like is a state verb not used in the continuous; ✗ have liked — plural, and the present perfect makes no sense for a general preference.

items.q: My cousin has ______ the piano and practises every evening after dinner.
items.vi: Em họ tôi mới bắt đầu học đàn piano và luyện tập mỗi tối sau bữa ăn.
items.explanation: Take up = start a new hobby or activity, which fits practises every evening. ✗ taken over — take control of a company or a job; ✗ taken in — understand something, or give someone a home; ✗ taken off — remove clothes, or leave the ground (a plane).

items.q: The chocolate cake ______ by my grandmother was the best thing at the party.
items.vi: Chiếc bánh sô-cô-la do bà tôi làm là món ngon nhất trong bữa tiệc.
items.explanation: A past participle shortens the passive relative clause which was made by my grandmother to the cake made by; the clue is the passive agent by my grandmother. ✗ making — a present participle would mean the cake did the making, which is impossible; ✗ was made — a full verb here would give the sentence two main verbs (was made … was); ✗ had made — active past perfect, it also makes a second main verb and says the cake made something.

items.q: This time next week we ______ on the beach in Nha Trang with all our cousins.
items.vi: Giờ này tuần sau chúng tôi sẽ đang nằm trên bãi biển Nha Trang cùng tất cả anh chị em họ.
items.explanation: This time next week points to an action in progress at a future moment, which takes the future continuous: will be lying. ✗ lie — present simple is for habits or timetables, not a picture of one future moment; ✗ have lain — present perfect links the past to now, not to next week; ✗ were lying — past continuous describes a past moment, but the time marker is future.

items.q: On the first day in Hue, my family went ______ and took photos of every old palace.
items.vi: Ngày đầu tiên ở Huế, gia đình tôi đi tham quan và chụp ảnh mọi cung điện cổ.
items.explanation: Go sightseeing is the set expression for visiting the famous places of a town, and took photos of every old palace confirms it. ✗ watching — needs an object (watching a film), and go watching is not a set phrase; ✗ viewing — also needs an object, and it is used for houses or exhibitions, not tours; ✗ looking — go looking must be followed by for something.

items.q: My brother and I often cook dinner ______ when our parents work late.
items.vi: Anh em tôi thường tự nấu bữa tối khi bố mẹ đi làm về muộn.
items.explanation: My brother and I = we, so the reflexive is ourselves, here meaning "without our parents' help". ✗ ourself — not a standard English form; the plural is always ourselves; ✗ themselves — refers to they, not to we; ✗ each other — a reciprocal pronoun, it would mean we cook one another, which makes no sense.

items.q: Could you ______ a photo of us in front of the cinema, please?
items.vi: Bạn chụp giúp bọn mình một tấm ảnh trước rạp chiếu phim được không?
items.explanation: Photo collocates with take: you take a photo / a picture. ✗ make — a direct translation from many languages, but English uses make for creating things (a cake, a film), not photos; ✗ do — pairs with tasks (homework, housework), never with a photo; ✗ catch — goes with a bus, a ball or a cold, not a photo.

items.q: Let's watch a comedy tonight, ______?
items.vi: Tối nay chúng ta xem phim hài nhé?
items.explanation: A suggestion with Let's always takes the tag shall we?. ✗ will we — will you? is the tag after an imperative (Open the door, will you?), not after Let's; ✗ do we — follows a negative present simple statement (We don't …, do we?); ✗ don't we — follows a positive present simple statement (We watch …, don't we?), but Let's is not a statement.
